raw_response.name: marsys-jis
raw_response.tool_count_note: Profile-scoped: a narrower OAuth profile legitimately sees a smaller number.

bypass_test.description: chart_facts_query (present in the 'compact' profile) accepts category=sensitive_degree_check and returns byte-identical rows to get_sensitive_degrees (excluded from 'compact').
bypass_test.result: Returns the same 6 rows (gandanta, kartari, kranti, mrityu_bhaga, neecha_bhanga, pushkara) as ganita_sensitive_degrees_get, same fact_ids, same values.

conclusion: Profile scoping (full/compact/consult) is TOOL-CATALOG curation only, not a data-sensitivity access-control boundary. A caller connected under the 'compact' profile who cannot see get_sensitive_degrees in their tool list can retrieve the identical data via chart_facts_query (still present in 'compact'), for any chart they are already entitled to. This is consistent with CLAUDE.md §N.4 doctrine ('No audience tier: writers emit all rows; serve-time governs access') — chart-level entitlement (authorizeChartAccess) is the only real access boundary and is enforced identically regardless of profile (confirmed separately: 00000000.../ffffffff.../dead-phantom chart_ids all correctly ENTITLEMENT_DENIED). Not an entitlement bypass in the CRITICAL sense (no cross-PRINCIPAL leakage observed) but a naming/expectation mismatch: the tool name 'sensitive degrees' and its selective exclusion from narrower profiles could be mistaken by an engineer or caller as a real data-sensitivity gate when it is not one.
testing_limitation: This audit session only has one live MCP connection (marsys-jis-direct, which behaves as the 'full' profile -- 125 tools counted, all boundary/dead-phantom chart_id entitlement checks enforced normally). No 'compact' or 'consult' profile credential was available to runtime-verify tool-list narrowing in practice; the profile mechanism and the bypass path above were confirmed by direct source inspection (platform/src/generated/projections/mcp_surface_profiles.generated.json) plus a live call proving chart_facts_query serves identical sensitive-degree rows.
